Physicl raises $10 million for Studio synthetic training environments

The platform repurposes 3D commerce tooling for physical-AI training data; Studio remains in private beta.

TechCrunch ↗6 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

A new use for a 3D pipeline

Physicl raised $10 million in seed funding led by Inovia Capital, TechCrunch reports. Founder Alex de Vigan is adapting experience from nfinite’s 3D commerce-rendering pipeline to robot and world-model training, aiming for representations with suitable geometry, materials and physics.

Targeting difficult examples

Studio is described as offering 10,000 3D environments and 100,000 assets. Users can construct cases such as a cup on a cluttered or shadowed counter, producing targeted post-training examples rather than relying solely on recorded footage or teleoperated robot data.

Early collaboration, limited access

SpAItial is an early customer collaborating on higher-fidelity data. Physicl’s website labels Studio a private beta requiring access requests. Neither the funding nor the asset count proves that the sim-to-real gap is solved; improvement still needs measurement on physical robots.
